linux.summary: No in-tree driver binds this PCIe part; b43 and brcmfmac do not cover 14e4:43a0. Wi-Fi requires Broadcom's proprietary out-of-tree wl driver (the broadcom-sta / bcmwl / broadcom-sta-dkms package), built per-kernel via DKMS. This is the most common Linux dealbreaker on these iMacs, and it carries Secure Boot implications.

caveats.summary: The wl module is unsigned, so it will not load while UEFI Secure Boot is enabled.
caveats.detail: Either enrol a Machine Owner Key (MOK) and sign the DKMS module, or disable Secure Boot. Out of the box the interface simply does not appear under Secure Boot.

caveats.summary: The stock broadcom-sta source fails to build on kernel 6.17 and newer.
caveats.detail: cfg80211/wireless API changes and removed helpers break the old driver source; distributions have shipped patched revisions and community forks carry the fixes. Relevant here because the reference iMac17,1 runs kernel 7.0.

workarounds.cause: Only the proprietary wl driver supports this chip and it is not installed by default.
workarounds.fix: Install the distribution's Broadcom STA package (Debian/Ubuntu: broadcom-sta-dkms / bcmwl-kernel-source; Arch: broadcom-wl-dkms), which builds wl via DKMS and blacklists the conflicting b43/bcma/ssb modules. Wired or USB tethering is needed for the initial install.

workarounds.problem: wl fails to compile on kernel 6.17+.
workarounds.fix: Use a distribution revision or a community fork of broadcom-sta that carries the kernel 6.17+ build patches.
